consensus_summary: Name symbolizes the essential character, identity, authority, presence, and power of the person who bears it (supremely God or Jesus), so that invoking or acting in the name engages the person himself; complementary facets include delegated authority, reputation, temple presence, and new/eschatological identity.
book_summary: Name is the covenant identity of a house, consisting specifically of its Head’s Word, covenant law, and fruitful priesthood; substituting any element yields a counterfeit and rejecting any takes the Name in vain.
consensus_core_identification: the revealed character/identity/authority/presence of a person (esp. God/Jesus)
book_core_identification: covenant identity of a house = Head’s Word + covenant law + fruitful priesthood
boundary_disagreement: Book introduces an entirely new composite referent (triadic contents of the house/ark as the Name itself) never listed among consensus primary or alternative meanings; consensus boundaries concern personal attributes or delegated uses, not this structural triad.
material_contradiction: None direct; the book does not explicitly deny the common personal-character reading (it even notes it) but simply replaces it with an unshared identification.
rationale: Minimum cores differ in referent: consensus centers on personal essence/authority; the book centers on a covenantal house-composition drawn from ark furnishings. No consensus response or alternative mentions Word + law + priesthood as constitutive of Name, so the identification is absent rather than a narrowing, broadening, or contradiction of a shared core.
strongest_objection: The printed texts associate ‘name’ with the house/ark and list the three ark items, yet never equate the Name itself to that triad; the definition therefore appears imposed rather than read out of the citations alone.
